description:
Follow-on surface T-011/T-013 need from the (complete, shipped) T-010 store, per N-007/N-008. Five items, all small, all in src/snapshot:

1. **assertGenerationInvariants** (closes ISS-064, hard prerequisite for item 2): body-shape validation for GenerationDoc mirroring assertManifestInvariants — provenance present with coverage array, sourceVersion canonicalizable, payload present — called at EVERY generation decode (classifyStore, readSnapshot, readGeneration). Per the mutation discipline, a test observes it refusing a checksum-valid/body-malformed generation, which today classifies "usable" and serves.

2. **readGeneration(id)**: read one generation by id, limited to ids that are manifest-retained or pinned; full envelope + invariant validation; NOT manifest-following (readSnapshot stays the only manifest-follower). This is the reader half of the pin mechanism T-013's cursors consume.

3. **Dominance amendments** (N-008 1a/1b): publishSnapshot gains retireSources — dominance permits a missing key ONLY when explicitly retired by the caller; unattested absence stays incomparable/fail-closed. publishSnapshot gains {status:"unchanged"} for candidate-equals-live, distinct from published and refused. Tests observe: an unattested missing source still refuses; an attested retirement publishes and logs; equal watermark reports unchanged, never published.

4. **sourceVersion semantics rewrite** (N-007 decision 1): contracts, comments and tests move from consumed-offset language to verified-input-watermark language (per-source newest event reflected in output). The consumed-offset ideal is EXPLICITLY deferred to the v0.5 owned-parsing ticket.

5. **ccusageFetchedAt -> ccusageInvokedAt** (N-007 decision 2, N-008 2a): rename, keep required, document as the invocation instant. KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, accepted: exact-key schema change — a pre-rename snapshot fails assertExactKeys and classifies to reset. Pre-release this is fine; it is written here so nobody discovers it.

Non-goals: no new authority semantics, no lease resurrection (cut per N-007 decision 4), no migration machinery (derived cache: reset is the migration).


## RE-SPECIFIED 2026-08-04 (N-009, docs/snapshot-facts-and-watermarks.md v2)

Items 3-4 above are superseded by the v2 contract: recency/coverage split, ingestion-surface registry (six surfaces), per-surface row identities and disappearance policies, published/refreshed/unchanged/refused outcomes, SnapshotPayloadV1 with producer totals and canonical ordering, writer-side codex attribution, and a size measurement against MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES as a PLAN-PHASE gate. The plan phase MUST take docs/snapshot-facts-and-watermarks.md and codex review session 019fcfc4 as inputs and resume that session for its plan review. Items 1 (assertGenerationInvariants) and 2 (readGeneration) stand as written; item 5 (ccusageInvokedAt) stands with its written-down reset consequence.

park.reason:
PARKING T-025 after 3 plan-review rounds and 30 findings (30 valid, 0 contested). The defect is in the FILING, and it is specifically this: ITEM 4 INSTRUCTS WRITING DOWN A DEFINITION THAT HAS NOT BEEN COMPLETED, AND ITEMS 3a/3b CANNOT BE SOUND IN ISOLATION FROM IT.

THE CONTRADICTION, precisely. Item 4 says to move contracts, comments and tests to 'verified-input-watermark language (per-source newest event reflected in output)'. That sentence cannot be executed as written, for two independent reasons, each verified against the code:

(1) 'PER-SOURCE' HAS NO DEFINED KEY DOMAIN. sourceVersion is Record<string, number> (types.ts:303); compareSourceVersions treats keys as opaque strings (dominance.ts:161-190); nothing anywhere binds what a key MEANS. Shipped tests use provider-like keys ({claude:10}, {claude:20, gemini:1}) while the only per-entity ccusage surface, claude daily --instances, is per PROJECT. N-007 decision 1 and N-008 1a both reason about 'sources' throughout and neither defines one. Filed as ISS-082 (critical).

(2) 'NEWEST EVENT REFLECTED IN OUTPUT' HAS NO ESTABLISHED WITNESS, and whether it has one DEPENDS on (1). Under provider keys, ccusage blocks --json is Claude-only so its actualEndTime is a genuine per-source sub-day signal for Claude and the problem shrinks to Codex. Under project keys, blocks carries no project key and the signal is global, which N-008 1a explicitly rejected. Filed as ISS-081 (critical), now rewritten twice and explicitly blocked on ISS-082.

Writing either sentence down before those are answered means recording a claim the store cannot support - which is exactly what RULES.md L-006 forbids, and L-006 is a stated constraint. An acceptance criterion that contradicts a stated constraint is the park criterion.

WHY NOT JUST SPLIT AND LAND THE REST - the question I pushed on for three rounds and was wrong about. I proposed a landing subset each round and it shrank every round as new coupling to item 4 surfaced: round 2 removed the candidate-side dominance rows (they are justified ONLY by the watermark redefinition item 4 holds); round 3 removed retirement-only (returning `dominates` for an attested topology change alters the transition relation dominance.ts currently documents, and that documentation IS item 4). The trend is the finding: any dominance change requires the semantics text, and the semantics text is undischargeable. I kept asserting a separation the reviewer kept disproving.

T-011 cost seven rounds by not parking when the pattern was legible at round four. This is round three.

WHAT THE OWNER SHOULD DO - the ticket needs SPLITTING, not just re-planning:

A. RE-FILE THE DISCHARGEABLE SUBSET as its own ticket. It is fully specified in the preserved plan and needs no owner decision: (i) close ISS-064 with the audit evidence - assertGenerationInvariants ALREADY EXISTS at store.ts:1014 and is called at all three sites (664 classify, 2699 read, 2206 write), with ten tests, so the ticket's item 1 is already shipped and its cited lines are stale; (ii) readGeneration(id), the piece T-013's AC 4 actually needs; (iii) the ccusageFetchedAt -> ccusageInvokedAt rename, store-contract only, whose witness demonstrably CAN exist (the invoking process knows when it spawned ccusage) and is deferred to T-011; (iv) delete PublishResult's uninhabited `refused` member. That subset unblocks T-013's cursor contract without touching dominance.

B. HOLD THE DOMINANCE/SEMANTICS SUBSET (items 3a, 3b, 4 and the candidate-side rows) behind ISS-082 then ISS-081, in that order. ISS-082 is the prior question - it changes ISS-081's answer rather than merely informing it.

PLAN PRESERVED at docs/t025-store-follow-on-plan.md (363 lines) - .story/sessions/ is gitignored, so that copy is the only one that survives. It carries the full readGeneration design (six-status result type, the seven-step pin authorization pass, the manifest/pin precedence rule), a 14-row dominance truth table marked by what lands when, and ~35 tests each naming the mutation that must kill it. Re-filing A is a copy, not a redesign.

NOT PARKED FOR: difficulty, review fatigue, or context. Seven of round 3's ten findings are ordinary fixable specifics and I could have produced revision 4. The three that matter cannot be fixed by planning.
